1-2.word_for_word: pañcame — in the fifth chapter; jātakam — the birth ceremony; nandaḥ — Nanda; sūnoḥ kṛtvā — having performed for his son; mahotsavam — a great festival; gatvā atha mathurām — then going to Mathurā; prāpa vasudeva-āgama-utsavam — he obtained the joy of Vasudeva’s coming; mahā-manāḥ — great-minded; udāra-cittaḥ — generous-hearted; verse 2 — na vyākhyātam, not explained.
1-2.translation: In the fifth chapter Nanda performs the birth ceremony and a great festival for his son; afterward he goes to Mathurā and receives the joy of meeting Vasudeva. ‘Mahā-manāḥ’ means generous-hearted. Śrīdhara gives no separate explanation for verse 2.

3.word_for_word: niyute — two hundred thousand; dve lakṣe — two lakhs; sapta tila-parvatān ca prādāt — he also gave seven mountains of sesame; ratna-oghiaiḥ — with masses of jewels; śātakaumbha-ambaraiḥ — with garments worked or dyed with gold; āvṛtān — covered.
3.translation: ‘Niyute’ means two lakhs. Nanda also gave seven mountains of sesame, covered with masses of jewels and with cloth enriched with gold.

4.word_for_word: dravyāṇām go-hiraṇya-ādīnām madhye — among possessions such as cows and gold; keṣāñcit dānaiḥ eva śuddhiḥ — some are purified specifically by charity; anna-dāna-ādi-yukta-jāta-karma-ādi-saṁskāraiḥ — through rites such as the birth ceremony accompanied by gifts of food and the like; garbhāṇām śuddhiḥ — purification of birth or offspring; pratiniyatāni śodhakāni — specifically assigned purifying means; kālena bhūmy-ādi — land and similar things by time; snānena deha-ādi — the body by bathing; śaucena amedhya-lipta-ādi — things soiled by impurity through cleansing; saṁskāraiḥ garbha-ādi — birth and offspring by purificatory rites; tapasā indriya-ādi — the senses by austerity; ijyayā brāhmaṇa-ādi — brāhmaṇas and sacred relations by worship; dānaiḥ dravya-ādi — possessions by charity; santuṣṭyā manaḥ — the mind by contentment; ātmā ātma-vidyayā — the self by knowledge of the Self.
4.translation: Śrīdhara gives the verse as a list of specifically assigned means of purification. Land and similar things are purified by time; the body by bathing; things touched by impurity through cleansing; birth and offspring by the prescribed saṁskāras; the senses by austerity; brāhmaṇas and sacred relations by worship; possessions such as cows and gold by charity; the mind by contentment; and the self by knowledge of the Self. The point here is that the birth rites, accompanied by gifts such as food, purify the birth just as charity purifies certain possessions.

5.word_for_word: saumaṅgalya-giraḥ — speakers of auspicious words; svasti-vācakāḥ — reciters of blessings; viprādayaḥ — the brāhmaṇas and others; sūtāḥ — Sūtas; paurāṇikāḥ — reciters of the Purāṇas; māgadhāḥ — Māgadhas; vaṁśa-śaṁsakāḥ — reciters of dynastic praise; vandinaḥ — bards; amala-prajñāḥ — of clear intelligence; prastāva-sadṛśa-uktayaḥ — speaking suitably to the occasion.
5.translation: ‘Saumaṅgalya-giraḥ’ means those who utter auspicious blessings. Śrīdhara identifies the Sūtas as reciters of Purāṇic histories, the Māgadhas as reciters of dynastic praise, and the Vandins as clear-minded bards whose words suit the occasion.

6.word_for_word: sammṛṣṭāni saṁsiktāni ca — swept clean and sprinkled with water; dvārāṇi — the doorways; ajirāṇi aṅganāni — the courtyards; gṛhāntarāṇi gṛha-madhyāni — the interiors of the houses; citra-dhvajāḥ — variegated banners; patākāḥ — flags; srajaḥ — garlands; caila-pallava-toraṇāni — gateways decorated with cloth and fresh leaves; taiḥ bhūṣitaḥ — adorned with all these.
6.translation: The doorways, courtyards and interiors of the houses were swept and sprinkled clean. Vraja was adorned with variegated banners and flags, garlands, cloth, fresh leaves and decorated gateways.

7.word_for_word: haridrā-tailaiḥ rūṣitāḥ — smeared with turmeric and oil; liptāḥ — anointed; vicitra-dhātavaḥ — various colored mineral decorations; barha-srajaḥ — peacock-feather garlands; vastrāṇi — cloths; kāñcana-mālāḥ — golden necklaces; alaṅkāratayā vidyante — present as ornaments; tathā-bhūtāḥ gavādayaḥ — the cows, bulls and calves were so decorated.
7.translation: The cows, bulls and calves were anointed with turmeric and oil and decorated with varied mineral colors, peacock-feather garlands, cloth and golden necklaces.

10.word_for_word: nava-kuṅkuma-kiñjalkaiḥ — with fresh saffron-pollen; mukha-paṅkajeṣu — upon their lotus-like faces; bhūtiḥ śrīḥ — beauty and splendor; yāsām tāḥ — those women whose faces possessed such beauty.
10.translation: Their lotus-like faces shone beautifully with fresh saffron-colored decoration.

15-16.word_for_word: tebhyaḥ prādāt — he gave these things to them; yathocitam — as was appropriate; anyān api apūjayat — he also honored the others in the fitting manner.
15-16.translation: Nanda gave the garments, ornaments, cows and other gifts to the Sūtas, Māgadhas, Vandins and others, and he also honored everyone else in the manner appropriate to each.

18.word_for_word: hareḥ nivāsena — because of Hari’s residence there; ye ātmani guṇāḥ — the qualities that arose in the place itself; sarva-priyatva-ādayaḥ — such as becoming dear to everyone; taiḥ — by those qualities; ramāyāḥ ākrīḍam — a playground of Ramā, Lakṣmī; vihāra-sthānam — a place of her sport.
18.translation: Because Hari resided there, Vraja acquired qualities such as becoming dear to everyone, and thus became a playground and place of delight for Ramā, the goddess of fortune.

19.word_for_word: vārṣikyam — annual; prati-varṣam deyam — payable every year; karam — tax or tribute.
19.translation: ‘Vārṣikyam’ means the tribute that was due each year.

20.word_for_word: bhrātaram — brother; sakhāyam — intimate friend; tad-avamoceanam — literally his release/place of dismounting; tasya nandasya vasati-sthānam — the place where Nanda was staying.
20.translation: Here ‘brother’ is used in the sense of intimate friend. ‘Tad-avamoceanam’ means the lodging place where Nanda was staying after arriving in Mathurā.

24.word_for_word: punar-bhavaḥ — born again; punar-jātaḥ iva — as though one had been born anew; saṁsāra-cakre vartamānaḥ — while moving in the wheel of saṁsāra; hetu-garbham viśeṣaṇam — this qualifying phrase contains the reason for the rarity of their meeting.
24.translation: ‘Punar-bhavaḥ’ means ‘as though born again.’ The phrase ‘while moving in this wheel of saṁsāra’ explains why obtaining the rare sight of a beloved friend again is so extraordinary.

25.word_for_word: durlabhatvam eva āha — he explains why such companionship is rare; priyaḥ ca asau saṁvāsaḥ ca — beloved companionship; he priya iti vā — or it may be read as an address, ‘O dear one’; srotasaḥ oghena nīyamānānām — carried by the flood of a current; plavāḥ tṛṇa-kāṣṭa-ādayaḥ — floating things such as grass and wood; teṣām yathā ekatra sthitiḥ na asti — just as they do not remain together in one place; tadvat — so it is with friends in saṁsāra.
25.translation: Śrīdhara explains the rarity of lasting companionship. Friends in saṁsāra are like floating pieces of grass and wood carried along by a river’s current: for a time they meet, but they cannot remain together in one place.

26.word_for_word: paśavya-ādi-rūpe tasmin vane — regarding whether that forest was suitable for cattle and otherwise prosperous; nirdoṣa-gopa-yaśodā-ādi-prabhūta-gopikā-stanya-ādinā — through the faultless cowherds, Yaśodā, the other abundant cowherd women and their milk; putra-kṣema-vivakṣayā pṛcchati — he asks indirectly with the intention of learning the welfare of his son; prasakta-dhīḥ sva-ātmajayoḥ iti uktatvāt — because the text has already said that his mind was absorbed in the two sons.
26.translation: By asking whether the forest was healthy, rich in water and grass and suitable for cattle, Vasudeva was indirectly asking about his son’s welfare—about Yaśodā, the other cowherd women, their milk and the whole environment that sustained the child. The text has already said that his mind was absorbed in the two boys.

27.word_for_word: bhavadbhyām upalālitaḥ san — while being lovingly raised by the two of you; kaccit vartate — is he doing well?; iti śeṣaḥ — this is the implied completion of the sentence.
27.translation: The implied completion is: ‘Is my son doing well while being lovingly raised by the two of you?’

28.word_for_word: putra-adarśana-kleśān āha — he speaks of the pain caused by not seeing one’s child; suhṛdaḥ bandhūn prati — toward friends and relatives; anubhāvitaḥ sampāditaḥ tri-vargaḥ — dharma, artha and kāma made effective for them; saḥ hi puṁsaḥ vihitaḥ — that alone is properly ordained for a person; śāstreṇa vā proktaḥ — or prescribed by scripture; na sva-mātra-paryavasitaḥ — not terminating in oneself alone; teṣu kliśyamāneṣu — while one’s loved ones suffer; sukhāya na bhavati — the three aims do not result in happiness.
28.translation: Vasudeva speaks of the pain of separation from one’s child. The three worldly aims—dharma, artha and kāma—are properly fulfilled when they are made beneficial to one’s friends and relatives, not when they end in oneself alone. If those dear to us are suffering, these three aims cannot bring real happiness.

29.word_for_word: nandaḥ vasudevam sāntvayan — Nanda, consoling Vasudeva; āha — said; aho iti — with the words beginning ‘alas.’
29.translation: Nanda now speaks in order to console Vasudeva for the loss of Devakī’s children.

30.word_for_word: adṛṣṭe eva niṣṭhā samāptiḥ yasya — one whose outcome rests in unseen destiny; putra-ādi-sukha-pradam adṛṣṭam hīyate — when the unseen merit producing the happiness of children and the like is exhausted; tadā te putrādayaḥ na bhavanti — then those children and blessings are no longer present; adṛṣṭa-paramaḥ — one for whom destiny is the determining factor; adṛṣṭam eva punaḥ saṅgamayati — the unseen power can again bring separated persons together; adṛṣṭam ātmanaḥ tattvam — this unseen destiny is the unfailing cause of one’s experiences; avyabhicāri-kāraṇam sukha-duḥkhayoḥ — the unfailing cause of happiness and suffering; yaḥ veda saḥ na muhyati — one who knows this is not bewildered; mṛtānām api viyuktānām api ca kālāntare darśana-yogayoḥ sambhavāt — even those dead or separated may be seen or united again at another time; nandasya daivī vāk bhāvi-sūcikā — Nanda’s divinely inspired words hint at what will occur later.
30.translation: Nanda says that a person’s circumstances rest upon unseen destiny. When the unseen merit that gives the happiness of children and other blessings is exhausted, those blessings disappear; the same unseen power can later bring separated persons together again. One who understands this unfailing causal relation behind happiness and suffering is not bewildered. Śrīdhara adds that Nanda’s words are divinely inspired and foreshadow the future reunion of those who have been separated.

31.word_for_word: tām buddhvā — understanding Nanda’s divinely suggestive words; vasudevaḥ duḥkham tyaktvā — Vasudeva put aside his grief; nandam āha — and spoke to Nanda; karaḥ vai iti — with the words beginning ‘the tax has indeed been paid’; vaḥ — by you, by all of you.
31.translation: Understanding Nanda’s words, Vasudeva put aside his grief and urged him to leave. In the phrase about the annual tax, ‘vaḥ’ means ‘by you all.’
